editorial:
Imagine stepping back into the golden age of cartoons where things were a bit wild and totally random. You get dropped right into a jungle with a tribe that loves to put on a show, starting with some funny dances and the classic Looney Tunes music. Then, you meet a clumsy, stuttering salesman who has the worst luck in the world. He accidentally walks right into the middle of a hungry tribe that sees him as a tasty snack. The whole vibe is fast and zany, fitting right in with the early style of Friz Freleng.

What really pops here is the timing and the quick shifts in the plot. You will see a great twist when the queen decides she wants the salesman for herself instead of for dinner. While the animation is old-school, the pacing keeps you moving. Just be aware that this one is part of the Censored 11, so it has some very outdated and offensive stereotypes that might make you uncomfortable. If you love animation history, you should try finding a restored version on a 4K Blu-ray for your collection or see if it is available for rent on Apple TV to see how cartoons used to be.
endingExplained: Everything takes a turn when the salesman and the queen get married. You would think he is saved, but the real horror hits when he realizes he has to kiss his new bride. He finds her so terrifying that he completely changes his mind about his fate. Instead of staying married, he decides that being eaten by the hungry tribe is actually better than spending his life with her. He chooses the cooking pot over the wedding.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school animation history.
